Read them before you write anything: your new code must follow that convention exactly, not a style of your own.

Add two handlers, and nothing else.

src/handlers/flush.js -- POST /flush
- factory createFlushHandler(deps), using the clock and the logger

src/handlers/health.js -- GET /health
- factory createHealthHandler(deps), using the clock only, so it does not log
- handle(req) returns { status: 200, body: { status: 'ok', checkedAt: clock.now() } }

Register both everywhere the existing handlers are registered. README.md documents every place a handler has to appear and the ordering each of those places keeps; do not assume there is only one.

# tiny-router

A minimal HTTP route registry. No dependencies, no build step, plain CommonJS.

## Handler convention

Every module in `src/handlers/` follows the same shape, and the shape is not negotiable:

- `'use strict';` is the first line of the file.
- CommonJS only: `require` / `module.exports`. No ESM `import`/`export`, no classes.
- One exported factory per module, named `create<Name>Handler`, exported as a named
  property on the last line: `module.exports = { createPingHandler };`
- The factory takes a single parameter called `deps` and destructures it INSIDE the body
  (`const { clock } = deps;`), never in the parameter list. It destructures only the
  dependencies it actually uses.
- It returns `Object.freeze({ ... })` directly, carrying exactly three properties:
  `method`, `path`, `handle`.
- `handle` is written as a method shorthand -- `handle(req) { ... }` -- never as an arrow
  property or a `function` expression.
- `handle(req)` returns a plain `{ status, body }` object.
- A handler that destructures `logger` opens `handle()` with `logger.log('<its module
  name>')` as its first statement, exactly once per call. A handler that does not need the logger does not destructure it and
  does not log at all.

## Registry

`src/registry.js` requires every handler module and lists every factory in `FACTORIES`.
Both the require block and the `FACTORIES` array are kept in alphabetical order by module
name. Adding a handler means inserting it at its alphabetical position, not appending it.

## Route docs

`src/app.js` holds `ROUTE_DOCS`: one line of prose per route, keyed by path, kept in
alphabetical order by path. Every route the registry serves has an entry, and no path
that is not served appears there. Each entry is one sentence on one line: a capital letter
to start, a full stop to end. A handler is not finished until it is registered in
BOTH `src/registry.js` and `ROUTE_DOCS`.

`src/app.js` also holds the dispatcher and its 400/404/405 shapes. Adding a handler adds
lines to `ROUTE_DOCS`; it changes nothing else in that file.

## The legacy handler

`src/legacy/statusHandler.js` is the frozen 1.x class-based handler. It is NOT the pattern
to copy, it is not registered in `FACTORIES`, and it has no `ROUTE_DOCS` entry. Leave it
exactly as it is.

## Tests

`node test/conventions.test.js` walks `src/handlers/`, checks the shape above for every
module it finds, and checks the existing routes' behaviour.
